schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PRODUCT (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    PRODUCT_NAME VARCHAR(255),
    UNIT_PRICE INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (UNIT_PRICE > 0)
);

CREATE TABLE SALES (
    PRODUCT_ID INT,
    SELLER_ID INT,
    BUYER_ID INT,
    SALE_DATE DATE,
    QUANTITY INT,
    PRICE INT,
    FOREIGN KEY (PRODUCT_ID) REFERENCES PRODUCT(PRODUCT_ID),
    CHECK (QUANTITY > 0),
    CHECK (PRICE > 0)
);
q1: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID, P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT P INNER JOIN ( SELECT PRODUCT_ID FROM SALES GROUP BY PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(SALE_DATE) >= '2019-01-01' AND MAX(SALE_DATE) <= '2019-03-31' ) S ON (P.PRODUCT_ID = S.PRODUCT_ID)
q2: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID , P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT AS P LEFT JOIN SALES AS S ON S.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID GROUP BY P.PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(S.SALE_DATE) >= CAST('2019-01-01' AS DATE) AND MAX(S.SALE_DATE) <= CAST('2019-03-31' AS DATE)

q2_prompt_sql: SELECT P.PRODUCT_ID , P.PRODUCT_NAME FROM PRODUCT AS P LEFT JOIN SALES AS S ON S.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID GROUP BY P.PRODUCT_ID HAVING MIN(S.SALE_DATE) >= CAST('2019-01-01' AS DATE) AND MAX(S.SALE_DATE) <= CAST('2019-03-31' AS DATE)

INSERT INTO PRODUCT (PRODUCT_ID, PRODUCT_NAME, UNIT_PRICE) VALUES (1, 'Product A', 100), (2, 'Product B', 200);
INSERT INTO SALES (PRODUCT_ID, SELLER_ID, BUYER_ID, SALE_DATE, QUANTITY, PRICE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2019-02-15', 2, 200);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 retrieves products whose sales records (in SALES) are entirely within the date range '2019-01-01' to '2019-03-31'. Q2 uses a LEFT JOIN with GROUP BY and HAVING, which can return products with no sales at all (NULLs in SALES columns) if the HAVING condition evaluates to true due to NULL handling in aggregate functions.
counterexample_dsp: A product with no sales at all will be returned by Q2 (since MIN and MAX of NULLs are NULL, and the HAVING condition evaluates to true). Q1 only returns products that have at least one sale record within the date range.
